title: Power Automate: bring your own connection in attended and unattended cloud-triggered desktop flow runs
summary: The briefing accurately separates Microsoft's planned cloud-run capability from the embedding requirements documented today. Minor corrections should acknowledge the published baseline licensing and give the navigation to the desktop-flow list.

claims.claim: Today's documented cloud-initiated connector-action runs require the Power Automate v2 schema.
claims.quote:
To successfully invoke a desktop flow containing connector actions from a cloud flow, it must meet the following two requirements:
- The desktop flow must use the Power Automate v2 schema.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: Today's documentation requires a co-owner's desktop flow to have all connection references embedded for cloud-initiated runs.
claims.quote: If you're a co-owner of the flow, all of its connection references must be marked as embedded.

claims.claim: Embedded in desktop flow is a per-connection-reference setting.
claims.quote:
In the Connection references screen, view all of the connection references used in the flow.
4. Set the Embedded in desktop flow option to Yes to enable it.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Embedding or removing a reference requires ownership of the underlying connection.
claims.quote: You can only embed or remove connection references from a desktop flow if you own the underlying connection.

claims.claim: Other co-owners can manage only the connection references they added.
claims.quote: Other co-owners can only manage connection references they add.

claims.claim: Run-only users can currently run shared connector-action desktop flows only through the desktop console.
claims.quote: Users (run-only) can run flows shared with them only via Power Automate for desktop's console using their own connections.

claims.claim: Run-only users must supply their own connections for these shared flows.
claims.quote: Makers with user access on a shared desktop flow must always bring their own connections when they run the flow.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Each connection is specific to a user.
claims.quote: Each connection is specific to a user and requires authentication to ensure secure access to data and services.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Connector actions use an authenticated connection to access external services and act on their data.
claims.quote: In Power Automate, a connection refers to the authenticated link between Power Automate and an external service. This connection allows Power Automate to access and perform actions on data from various services

claims.claim: Connection authentication typically uses OAuth, API keys or another authentication method provided by the service.
claims.quote: This authentication is typically done using OAuth, API keys, or other authentication methods provided by the external service.

claims.claim: Sharing a desktop flow does not automatically grant access to its underlying connections.
claims.quote: Sharing a desktop flow does not automatically provide access to the underlying connections utilized.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; What's changing
claims.claim: Embedding a connection reference gives other co-owners access to the underlying data when modifying or running that desktop flow.
claims.quote: By embedding a connection reference to a desktop flow, you allow other co-owners to have access to the underlying data provided by it, for both modifying as well as running the desktop flow.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Connector actions can read and write service data through the underlying connection.
claims.quote:
The following actions are currently supported in desktop flows:
- Add a new row to selected environment
- Delete a row from selected environment
- Download a file or an image from selected environment
- Get a row by ID from selected environment

claims.claim: Importing a desktop flow with embedded references in a solution does not automatically include the required connection references.
claims.quote: When importing a desktop flow with embedded connection references in a solution, the required connection references aren't automatically included.

claims.claim: Microsoft's documented workaround is to include the required references explicitly alongside the flow in the solution.
claims.quote: To work around this current limitation, explicitly include the required connection references in the solution alongside the desktop flow.

claims.claim: Existing desktop-flow data policies classify action groups as business or non-business.
claims.quote: Power Automate offers administrators the option to create and enforce policies that classify desktop flows action groups as business or non-business and mark actions or action groups as blocked.

claims.claim: Existing desktop-flow data policies can block actions or action groups.
claims.quote: Apart from marking action groups as business and non-business, the administrator can mark action groups or particular actions as blocked. In this case, these actions can't be used at all in the flow.

claims.claim: A desktop flow suspended for a data-policy violation cannot run.
claims.quote: A desktop flow that violates a data loss prevention (DLP) policy will be marked as suspended and the run option will be disabled.

claims.claim: The suspended desktop flow cannot run through a cloud flow either.
claims.quote: For cases that a desktop flow is suspended, it won't be able to run it. Similarly, a cloud flow using a suspend desktop flow won't be able to run either.
